theme: The Isaiah Apocalypse, cosmic judgment and salvation
readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 24:1-27:13. These chapters are called the Isaiah Apocalypse. They look beyond the Assyrian crisis to the end of history. Read for the big picture: the whole earth judged, and a feast on the mountain of the LORD.
settingTheScene: After the oracles against individual nations, Isaiah steps back and describes judgment on the whole earth. The language is cosmic, with the earth laid waste, the heavens shaken, and the moon confounded. And in the midst of it, there are songs of praise, a banquet for all peoples, and the promise that death itself will be swallowed up. Though these chapters are difficult, they contain some of the most beautiful promises in the Bible.
observation: “Behold, the LORD will empty the earth and make it desolate, and he will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants” (24:1).
“The earth lies defiled under its inhabitants; for they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, broken the everlasting covenant” (24:5).
“O LORD, you are my God; I will exalt you; I will praise your name, for you have done wonderful things” (25:1).
“On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wine” (25:6).
“He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces” (25:8).
“You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you” (26:3).
“Your dead shall live; their bodies shall rise” (26:19).
“In that day the LORD with his hard and great and strong sword will punish Leviathan” (27:1).
interpretation:
Chapter 24 describes universal judgment. It falls on everyone: priest and people, master and servant, buyer and seller. The cause is that humanity has broken “the everlasting covenant.” This is not just Israel’s sin but the sin of the whole human race, going back to Adam and Noah. The earth itself suffers under the guilt of its inhabitants.

Yet scattered through the judgment are glimpses of praise. From the ends of the earth, songs of glory to the Righteous One are heard. And then in chapter 25, an extended song of thanks. God has been a stronghold to the poor and needy, a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat. He has done wonderful things, plans formed of old, faithful and sure.

The heart of the Apocalypse is Isaiah 25:6-9. On the mountain of the LORD, a feast is prepared for all peoples. This is not for Israel alone. It is the banquet of the kingdom. And the shroud that covers all peoples will be destroyed. “He will swallow up death forever.” God himself will wipe away tears from all faces. The disgrace of his people will be removed. And the people will say, “This is our God; we have waited for him, that he might save us.” The sight of death’s defeat is the central hope of the Old Testament.

Chapter 26 is a song for the day of salvation, and it contains the verse for this week: “You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you.” A mind fixed on God is a mind at rest. And verse 19, “Your dead shall live; their bodies shall rise,” is one of the clearest statements of resurrection in the Old Testament. Chapter 27 ends with the vineyard of Isaiah 5 restored: “Israel shall blossom and put forth shoots and fill the whole world with fruit.”
connection: Paul quotes Isaiah 25:8 in 1 Corinthians 15:54: “Death is swallowed up in victory.” Revelation 21:4 echoes: “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more.” Jesus told of the great banquet (Luke 14:15-24) and the wedding feast (Matthew 22:1-14). Revelation 19:9 speaks of the marriage supper of the Lamb. Philippians 4:7 speaks of the peace of God that guards our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
application:
Memorize Isaiah 26:3 and practice it when you feel anxious.

Think about someone who has died in Christ, and take comfort from the promise of resurrection.

Remember the banquet. Invite someone this week to a meal as a small picture of the feast.
prayerPrompts: Praise God for the wonderful things he has done.
Thank him that he will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears.
Tell him what tears you are bringing him.
